transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I've been feeling persistently depressed and sad for a very long time now, for about two and a half years. It just feels like this low mood has become a constant part of my life and never really goes away.
Have you had any periods lasting at least two weeks where your mood was clearly better, almost back to normal?
No, I don't really recall having any periods where my mood felt normal or better. It has just felt consistently low and heavy for this whole time.

latest_inference.note: Previously the candidates were ["Major Depressive Disorder", "Persistent Depressive Disorder"], but based on this conversation, Major Depressive Disorder is less likely because the patient reports a persistent low mood for over two years without significant periods of normal mood, which better aligns with Persistent Depressive Disorder. The absence of a two-week remission period rules out full remission in Major Depressive Disorder and supports the chronic nature of Persistent Depressive Disorder.
